# Working at Redwood: Roles, Career Ladders, Benefits, Hiring & Onboarding, and Internal Tools

Short intro

Welcome to the canonical handbook page for what it means to work at Redwood. This page consolidates guidance on working culture, role definitions and career ladders, benefits and perks, the hiring and new-hire onboarding flow, and the core internal tools and access patterns you will rely on day-to-day. Use the sections below as quick references; teams should link to this page from team onboarding playbooks.

---

## 1. Our working culture (high level)

- Mission-aligned: prioritize customer-facing reliability and predictable inference economics.
- Engineering-first: we value shipping reliable systems, well-documented APIs, and measurable SLOs.
- Collaboration norms: asynchronous-first communication, documented decisions, and clear code ownership.
- Working model: distributed with core overlap hours (10:00–15:00 PT) for most teams; flexible schedules with manager approval.

## 2. Roles and career ladders

This section summarizes role families and progression expectations. Managers should link to team-specific ladders and promotion rubrics.

### Role families

- Engineering: Backend, Serving Runtime, Infra, SRE, Developer Experience
- Product: Product Management, Design, Data/Product Analytics
- Applied ML & Research: Model onboarding, evals, quantization research
- Platform & Security: Platform engineering, security & compliance
- GTM: Sales, Marketing, Customer Success, Solutions Engineering
- People & Ops: People Ops, Finance, Legal

### Career ladder summary (high level table)

| Level | Typical title examples | Focus / Expectations |
|---|---:|---|
| IC1 | Associate / New grad | Learning, task ownership, shipping small features, heavy mentorship |
| IC2 | Software Engineer / PM II | Independently deliver features, own medium complexity projects, reliable execution |
| IC3 | Senior Engineer / PM III | System design, cross-team coordination, mentoring juniors |
| IC4 | Staff / Principal | Technical leadership, platform-wide impact, shape roadmaps and standards |
| IC5 | Distinguished / Senior Principal | Strategic influence across company, industry-level contributions |

Notes: promotions require documented impact, manager support, and calibration with peers. People Ops runs semi-annual calibration cycles; teams should submit promotion packets per the Promotions playbook.

## 3. Benefits & perks (summary)

We offer a competitive benefits package designed for a distributed engineering-first company. Below is a concise table and additional notes. Reach out to benefits@redwood.com for policy details and enrollment windows.

| Category | What we provide | Notes / How to use |
|---|---|---|
| Health & wellbeing | Medical (PPO/HMO options), Dental, Vision | Redwood covers primary portion of employee premiums; dependents subsidized |
| Flexible time off | Unlimited PTO (guidelines), 10 paid holidays, 12 weeks parental leave | Manager coordination required; refer to Time Off policy for examples |
| Financial | 401(k) with company match, competitive equity grants, annual merit cycles | Eligibility begins on first day for 401(k) enrollment window |
| Learning & development | $2,000/year L&D stipend, conference budget, internal learning tracks | Submit requests through L&D portal (Confluence + Workday form) |
| Workspace & tools | Home office stipend, co-working allowances, preferred hardware program | Submit receipts via expenses workflow; see Hardware guide for approved models |
| Wellness & perks | Monthly wellness stipend, commuter benefits where applicable, team budgets | Teams responsible for budget allocation and reconciliation |

Benefits procedures (short)

1. Enroll in benefits within 30 days of start date via Workday benefits enrollment.
2. Submit L&D requests through the L&D form and cc your manager.
3. For parental leave, notify People Ops at least 60 days when possible; see Parental Leave policy for details on pay and job protection.

## 4. Hiring and onboarding overview

This section covers the candidate experience, interview practices, and the new-hire setup checklist. Hiring managers must follow the Hiring Scorecard template and inclusive interviewing guidelines.

### Hiring: process overview

1. Raise req via Greenhouse and attach a Hiring Scorecard; People Ops approves budget and role leveling.
2. Shortlist and screen: recruiter screens -> 1–2 hiring manager technical screens -> loop of 3–4 interviews (tech, system design, behavioral, cross-functional).
3. Calibration: team hiring debrief against scorecard; hiring manager writes justification for offer.
4. Offer & negotiation: People Ops extends official offer, handles background checks and documentation.

Interview standards & inclusivity

- Use consistent rubrics and anonymized rubric scoring where possible.
- Provide interview materials to candidates in advance (agenda, expectations).
- Offer interview-time accommodations (extended time, captioning, timezone considerations).

### New-hire onboarding (90-day view)

Phase-based checklist (owner abbreviations in parentheses):

1. Pre-boarding (Recruiter / People Ops)
   - Welcome email with start date, manager contact, first-week agenda.
   - Account provisioning request triggered for core systems (Okta, Google Workspace, Greenhouse access as needed).

2. Day 0–1 (Manager + People Ops + IT)
   - Hardware delivered and validated.
   - Access to OKTA, GitHub, Jira, Slack, Confluence, CI/CD dashboards.
   - First-week onboarding calendar and buddy assigned.

3. Week 1–4 (Manager + Team)
   - Complete role-specific short-running tasks: local dev setup, run sample PR, attend core product demos.
   - Kickoff 1:1 schedule and set initial goals.

4. Month 1–3 (Manager + Mentor)
   - Run a ramp plan with measurable milestones (e.g., take ownership of first bug or feature, contribute to design doc).
   - 30/60/90 check-ins and formal feedback at day 90.

Onboarding access checklist (required systems)

- Okta / SSO (primary identity)
- Google Workspace (email, calendar, Drive)
- Slack (team channels + private groups)
- GitHub (repo access: team + project repos)
- Jira (team boards)
- Confluence (team wiki + company handbook)
- CI/CD dashboards (read access), and request write access via PR to infra team
- Monitoring & alerting dashboards (read)

## 5. Internal tools guide (quick reference)

This is the short map to the most-used internal systems and ownership for access/integration. For detailed runbooks and API keys follow the tools team playbooks.

- Okta (Identity) — People Ops is owner; use to request app access.
- Google Workspace — People Ops + IT; Drive templates, org calendar.
- Slack — Eng-Platform owns standard channels and archived naming conventions.
- GitHub — Eng-Developer-Experience owns org-level permissions; repo ownership is declared in CODEOWNERS.
- Jira — Eng-Platform maintains templates and project schemes; PMs create boards for product teams.
- Confluence — People Ops + Eng-Platform; page templates available under /templates.
- CI/CD & Build (internal) — Eng-Infra owns build agents and secrets rotation; request via internal ticket queue.
- Observability (Dashboards & Alerts) — Eng-Platform owns dashboards; SRE owns PagerDuty schedules and escalation policies.

Access request flow (1–2 day SLA typical)

1. Submit an access request through the Access Request form (Confluence link + automated Slack bot).
2. App owner approves or requests more info.
3. Ops/IT completes provisioning and documents the change on the request ticket.

Secrets & credential hygiene

- All secrets must be stored in the company-managed vault (KMS/HSM-backed). Never share secrets in Slack or email.
- Rotate service credentials on the 90-day cadence unless otherwise documented.

## 6. Manager and team responsibilities

- Managers: run onboarding, set goals, maintain career development conversations every quarter, and submit promotion packets.
- Mentors/Buddies: provide day-to-day help for the new hire first 30 days.
- People Ops: policy owner for benefits, L&D, and hiring infrastructure.

## 7. FAQs and common procedures

- How do I request ergonomic equipment? -> Submit a Hardware request form and cc your manager.
- Where are promotion rubrics stored? -> See the Promotions playbook in Confluence (link).
- How do I report harassment? -> Follow the Harassment & Reporting procedure in the Security & Compliance space or contact People Ops confidentially.

## 8. Ownership and maintenance

- Document owner: People Ops (Sofia Patel).
- Review cadence: annual review in Q4 or sooner following policy changes or major org changes.
- Last major update: 2027-02-20 (policy refresh for parental leave and hardware programs).
